objective: Restore the production maintenance pipeline from repository refresh through a completed model-backed triage without weakening read or patch permissions.

changes.result: Reuse exact prior Git blobs, fetch only changed readable blobs, compact prompt-only system evidence, retain safe refresh errors, and bound deferred triage buffering.
Keep repository evidence reads on the readable boundary instead of routing them through the narrower patch boundary.
Send only inspectable repository paths to triage rather than every Git tree entry.

deployment.cleanup: Removed unused historical release image tags while retaining the active and immediate rollback images.

incidents_and_limits: The first deployed revision exposed a read-versus-write boundary mismatch; PR 45 corrected it before replaying the durable triage.
The next production payload exposed an unbounded all-tree path list; PR 46 restricted it to paths available to the inspection tool.

Two operator diagnostic probes launched a second Python process inside the 128 MiB maintenance container and caused one automatic container restart each. PostgreSQL and durable jobs were unaffected; later payload inspection used the 256 MiB API container.

This acceptance proves one current production triage reached and completed a real model call. It does not replay or reclassify all historical blocked jobs and does not certify general employee expertise.
